e: . This Psalm, while expressive of David's pious feelings on assuming the royal office, teaches the humble, submissive temper of a true child of God.
The form is that of an oath or strongest assertion. Submission is denoted by the figure of a weaned child. As the child weaned by his mother from the breast, so I still the motions of pride in me (
). Hebrew children were often not weaned till three years old.
may be taken for desire, which gives a more definite sense, though one included in the idea conveyed by the usual meaning, myself.
